heroHeadline: Mount Jack Fire Near Sooke Downgraded to 'Being Held' as Season Wind-Down Continues
heroSubtitle: The Mount Jack wildfire west of Sooke, BC was reclassified from 'out of control' to 'being held' on September 26 after rain cut fire behaviour to a smoldering Rank 1 the previous evening; the fire remains at 276.19 hectares with roughly 65 personnel assigned and no evacuation orders or alerts issued. It was one of only two fires still classified out of control provincewide as of September 25, when BC's active count stood at 100. The Northwest Territories' season has effectively wound down, its active count having collapsed to just 7 fires from 79 a week earlier. No new deaths, evacuation orders, or economic developments were identified this cycle.
